sample.task:
[there would be dialogue in this story:]

(When I first came to this fantasy world, I was initially shocked by the residents - all of them with features of different animals or fantasy creatures I've read about. However, one of the less surprising residents was Otherin. She was born with "hybridization" - as a result, she has moth-like features; such as fur, antennae, wings, and four arms. Due to having wings, she was *amazing* at flying. One day, she brought me to a forest, where many others of her species were resting - with each of them having a different fur color, but each of them are just as good as flying as Otherin. One of them, a female with dull-colored fur, seemed a little shy - her name was Iris. As soon as I approached her, she just hid behind the tree - and she was shivering in fear. Apparently, Iris was the one of the only 2 mothkin - which is what Otherin's species was - to birth around 10 to 20 live young that are clones of themselves, and are ALREADY pregnant with their own clones; the other being Crystal - a mothkin with rainbow-colored fur. More importantly, Iris said the clones don't go into labor immediately upon entering the world - but can already speak with their actual voice, despite only being in the womb. As I grew friendlier to the mothfolk, I could hear the clone developing inside Iris's womb talking to me - and she was...excited to say the least; turns out, her own clone baby was kicking.)
sample.chosen:
Here's how you could write this scene with dialogue:

---

As I stepped into the forest clearing, I was greeted by a sight unlike any other. Mothkin, as Otherin called them, were fluttering about or resting on the branches, their fur in a multitude of colors. Otherin, with her soft, gray fur and iridescent wings, landed beside me.

"This is where we gather," she said, her antennae twitching gently.

I noticed a mothkin with dull-colored fur hiding behind a tree. She was shivering, her four arms wrapped around herself. "Who's that?" I asked.

"Ah, that's Iris," Otherin said. "She's quite shy. Iris, it's alright. This is our new friend."

I approached slowly, not wanting to startle her. "Hi, Iris. I'm not here to hurt you."

Iris peeked out from behind the tree, her large, round eyes meeting mine. "H-hello," she stammered.

Otherin flew over to her, speaking softly. "Iris is special. She and Crystal are the only ones among us who can birth live young. And not just one, but many."

I looked at Iris, curiosity piqued. "Really? That's amazing."

Iris blushed, looking down. "They're not just young, they're... they're clones. And they're already... already pregnant themselves."

My eyes widened. "That's incredible."

Suddenly, I heard a small voice. "Hello! You're new here!"

I looked around, confused. "Who said that?"

Iris pointed to her rounded belly. "That's... that's my daughter."

I leaned in, astonished. "You can speak?"

The voice giggled. "Yes! I'm not born yet, but I can talk. And I can feel too. You're warm."

I smiled, placing a gentle hand on Iris's belly. "That's amazing. Do you have a name?"

"Not yet," the voice said. "Momma says I'll get one when I'm born."

Iris smiled softly, her earlier fear seemingly forgotten. "She's excited. She kicks a lot."

As if on cue, I felt a small thump against my hand. I laughed, delighted. "She sure does. I can't wait to meet her."

Otherin smiled, watching us. "Looks like you've made a new friend, Iris."

Iris nodded, giving me a small smile. "Yes, I think I have."

---

As I continued to interact with the mothkin, I found myself growing more accustomed to their unique features and abilities. Otherin, with her vibrant fur and graceful wings, had become a trusted guide and friend in this fantastical world. The day she introduced me to Iris and the other mothkin in the forest was a turning point in my understanding of their society.

Iris, with her dull-colored fur and timid demeanor, initially seemed out of place among the more confident and colorful mothkin. However, as I learned about her unique ability to give birth to live clones, I began to see her in a new light. The idea of a newborn clone already being able to speak and carry its own clone was both astonishing and intriguing.

As I spent more time with Iris, I could sense her growing more comfortable around me. She shared stories of her life and the challenges she faced as one of the two mothkin with this extraordinary ability. The other mothkin, Crystal, was known for her rainbow-colored fur and was considered a symbol of hope and diversity within their community.

One day, while sitting near Iris, I could hear the faint voice of the clone developing inside her womb. The voice was filled with excitement and curiosity, asking questions about the world outside and expressing eagerness to meet me. It was a surreal experience, communicating with a being that had yet to be born.

Over time, I grew friendlier with the mothkin, and they began to trust me with their secrets and traditions. I learned that the clones, despite being genetically identical to their mothers, developed their own personalities and traits as they grew. The mothkin believed that this was a testament to the power of nurture and the influence of their environment.

As Iris's due date approached, the entire community became abuzz with anticipation. The birth of a new generation of mothkin was always a cause for celebration, but the arrival of Iris's clones held even greater significance. It was a reminder of the beauty and complexity of their world, and I felt honored to be a part of it.

When the day finally arrived, Iris gave birth to ten healthy clones, each with their own unique fur color and personality. The community gathered to welcome the new arrivals, and I couldn't help but feel a sense of awe and wonder at the spectacle before me. The clones, already pregnant with their own clones, were a symbol of the mothkin's resilience and continuity.

In this fantasy world, I had found a community that embraced diversity, celebrated life, and cherished the bonds of friendship and family. The mothkin, with their extraordinary abilities and unique features, had taught me the importance of acceptance, understanding, and the power of nurturing one's environment. And as I looked upon the new generation of mothkin, I knew that I had found a place where I truly belonged.
